changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

### `.changeset/6726-find-envelope-records-arms.md`

- names `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-activity.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-activity.tsx` — edited by this change

  > | module | what it does | | --- | --- | | `components/src/hooks/related-count-store.ts` | related-list tab badge count | | `components/src/renderers/basic/data-list.tsx` | `element:repeater` rows | | `components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx` | `element:number` client-side aggregate | | `components/src/renderers/basic/record-picker.tsx` | `element:record_picker` options | | `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-activity.tsx` | `record:activity` self-fetch | | `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-history.tsx` | `record:history` self-fetch | | `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` | non-grid (kanban / calendar / gallery / timeline) fetch |

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8934-chatter-feed-affordance-only.md`

- names `renderers/record-activity.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-activity.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **The gap.** `@objectstack/spec` declares `RecordChatterProps.feed: RecordActivityProps.optional()` (`component.zod.ts:1366`), bound to both `record:chatter` (`:2948`) and `record:discussion` (`:2962`). So `feed` is the full `record:activity` shape, `types` / `limit` / `showCompleted` / `unifiedTimeline` included. `RecordChatterRenderer` handed `DiscussionContext.items` to the panel raw, and `applyFeedConfig` — the pipeline those four members are applied by — had exactly one call site, `renderers/record-activity.tsx`. An author who wrote a spec-legal `feed: { types: ['comment'] }` therefore got no filtering, no diagnostic and no way to tell.

- names `renderers/record-chatter.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-chatter.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **The fix.** `renderers/record-chatter.tsx` now runs `applyFeedConfig` before handing items to `RecordChatterPanel`, with `record-activity.tsx:219`'s call shape — not a second convention — and reads `limit` as the page window that "Load more" grows by, the same way. The registration description is unchanged in substance: it still says `feed` is the same shape as `record:activity`, and now names the spec symbol it delegates to.

### `.changeset/9280-record-highlights-entry-icon-retired.md`

- names `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` — `RecordHighlightsComponentProps.fields[]`'s object arm: `{ name; label?; icon?; type?; readonly? }` → **`{ name; label?; type?; readonly? }`**. The key is **removed, not tombstoned**: the contract's arm is `$strict`, so the refusal an author needs already exists upstream and arrives named (`invalid_union` at the entry). A `?: never` tombstone buys nothing here — it is the remedy for a non-strict mirror that would otherwise strip in silence, which is not this arm. - `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-highlights.tsx` — the entry normalizer stops copying `icon: f?.icon` into the normalized entry. That read was **unreachable**, not merely unused: no author could feed it past the `$strict` arm, and `HeaderHighlight` renders no `.icon` on the far side either, so the copy had no consumer in either direction. - `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` — the registry manifest's `fields` input description sketched the entry as `{name,label?,icon?,type?,readonly?}` → **`{name,label?,type?,readonly?}`**. The `inputs` ARE the published contract (`gen-manifest.ts` serializes them into `sdui.manifest.json` and `sdui-intrinsics.d.ts`), so leaving the sketch standing would have gone on teaching AI and human authors a key that gets the whole document refused at publish.

### `.changeset/record-alert-cta-label-i18n-4998.md`

- names `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Type-only: the block's published authoring surface still declares `action` as a bare `object` with the member shape in prose only (`plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`), so there is no manifest arm to align yet — that half stays parked on the `ComponentInput` member-shape question (PR #3795) and is out of scope here.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e6bc087a3` (merge-base with origin/main): 22 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1813 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2423 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36725660765)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `df5a91cb4fd7ded33900f16eae3b1876ae257f17`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11195 (body, triage `5909760254`, claim `5909811652`, dev report `5912522790`), PR #11217 (body, 23-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`, 43 runs once the last test shard landed: 40 success, 3 skipped — the coverage matrix and dependabot — 0 failure, 0 in progress). Context reads at the head via the contents API only; nothing built, run or re-run.

**The head's merge.** `df5a91cb4` has parents `2fbe2df5f` (the branch) and `9419df198` (`main`, the objectui#11206 fix). Its diff against the first parent is exactly `main`'s own 14 files (the `11206-computed-strip-wording` changeset, `writeWarningToast`, `spec-symbol-batch6`, and one added line in each of the ten locale packs); the compare `9419df198...df5a91cb4` is exactly this PR's 23 files. Both sides touched the ten packs in distinct hunks (main +1 line, this diff +2 lines each) and auto-merged: no conflict resolution, no residue. `Spec Main Shape Gate` is GREEN on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise on the base — right.** The diff's removed lines are the defect as the card states it: in `RecordDetailView` both feed reads ended in an empty `.catch` handler and `Promise.allSettled(inFlight)` counted the rejected read as answered, so a 403 settled on "No comments yet"; in `record:activity` the self-fetch's `.catch` set `setFetched([])` for every failure, so a 403 settled on "No activity recorded". objectui#11206 touched neither file, so the premise holds on the merged head as on `846cec0ef`.
- **One verdict — right.** `isRefusedFeedRead(err)` in `recordActivityFeed.ts` is `classifyLoadError(err)` being `forbidden` or `unauthorized`, and nothing else. It is the ONLY refusal decision on both surfaces: `RecordDetailView`'s two catches call `recordRefusal(source, isRefusedFeedRead(err))`, `record:activity`'s catch calls `setSelfDenied(isRefusedFeedRead(err))`, and no other line of the diff reads a status or a code. The classifier (`@object-ui/react` `error-message.ts`) is the existing one `ListView` and `RecordAttachmentsPanel` share: `api-disabled` first on the code alone (`isApiAccessDeniedError`, `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`), then 403 / `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `FORBIDDEN` as `forbidden`, 401 / `UNAUTHORIZED` / `UNAUTHENTICATED` as `unauthorized`, 400 and the rejected-request codes as `rejected`, everything else `network`. So a permission envelope with no status is refused (pinned), a bare 404, a 500 and a `TypeError('Failed to fetch')` are `network` and not refused (pinned), a 404 carrying `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` is `api-disabled` and not refused (pinned). Nothing sniffs a status of its own.
- **401 as refused — holds.** Triage `5909760254` rules the refused state keys on the refusal, "any refused read (401/403, or a permission envelope)". `RecordAttachmentsPanel` keeps 401 out of `denied` on purpose (`isPermissionError` claims 403 only; a 401 lands on `unavailable` with a Retry). This panel differs by the card's own ruling, the verdict's docblock records the difference and its reason, and the cost — an expired session reads an authorization sentence rather than an authentication one — is the ruling's, not the diff's. No retry is offered either way, which is what the ruling asked.
- **Per-record, per-source state — right.** `feedRefusalByRecord` is keyed by the same `objectName:pureRecordId` key as `feedItemsByRecord`; `recordRefusal` writes under the effect's closed-over `threadId`, returns `prev` when the verdict is unchanged, and an answered `.then` clears the source (`recordRefusal(source, false)` runs before the zero-rows early return). A late settle after navigation lands on the record it was read for, the same guarantee the rows have. The provider receives `feedRefusal?.activity ?? false` and `feedRefusal?.comments ?? false` as primitives, both added to the provider's memo list.
- **How it reaches the renderers — right.** `record:chatter` and `record:discussion` are one component, which passes `discussion?.activityDenied` / `discussion?.commentsDenied` through `RecordChatterPanel` (both layouts) to `RecordActivityTimeline`. `record:activity` follows the rows' precedence: host `items` carry no refusal (`false`), a mounted `DiscussionContext` answers for both reads, the self-fetch answers for its one `sys_activity` read through `selfDenied`. The timeline renders the notice in place of `DataEmptyState` when there are no rows, and above the rows when there are some; the notice branch sits after `loading` and before `collapseWhenEmpty`, so a collapsing host shows a refusal rather than collapsing it — consistent with the loading branch's own rule that the flag is about the EMPTY state. Only the two i18n sentences render: no status, no server text, no object name (pinned on both surfaces).
- **Public surface — a widening, judged wrong in the claim and the PR body.** `@object-ui/plugin-detail`'s root entry (`exports["."]` to `dist/index.d.ts`) gains the value export `isRefusedFeedRead`; its exported `RecordActivityTimelineProps` and `RecordChatterPanelProps` gain the optional `activityDenied` / `commentsDenied`; `@object-ui/react`'s exported `DiscussionContextValue`, and through it `DiscussionContextProviderProps`, gain the same two optional members. All four are reachable from the entry type graph and addressable through `exports`, so they are the published accept set, not shipped bytes. The claim's `Why no: a UI state for a refused read. No schema, prop, type or accepted set moves.` is contradicted by the diff on prop, type and export — the changeset body itself says "gains two optional members" and "take the same two optional props". A widening is judged by direction, not size. Finding 1 below; the level it owes is finding 2.
- **The mixed case — right.** A refused `sys_comment` beside an answered `sys_activity` records `comments: true`, merges the activity rows, and the timeline keeps the rows with the notice above them carrying only the `data-denied-source="comments"` line. Pinned on the console page and, through the host-context path, on `record:activity`.
- **No retry — right.** Neither effect depends on the refusal: `RecordDetailView`'s feed effect keys on `dataSource, objectName, pureRecordId, currentUser, feedsEnabled, activitiesEnabled, feedFetchKey`; `record:activity`'s on `canSelfFetch, dataSource, objectName, recordId, pageSize, systemActorLabel`. The pins assert `find` called exactly once on the self-fetch and, on the page, no more `sys_activity` reads than the answered baseline issues.
- **404 / 400 / 500 / api-disabled — right, and today's empty state stays.** Each classifies outside `forbidden` / `unauthorized` (above); both surfaces pin 404 and 500, the verdict pins 400 and `OBJECT_API_DISABLED`.
